key_points.point: The document articulates an ambition to develop superintelligence to tackle pressing global challenges and advance human civilization. It frames technology as the primary engine of human progress, seeking to accelerate human potential and achievement across science, commerce, medicine, and education. However, this accelerationist impulse is explicitly bounded by a commitment to human control and domestic safety constraints, distinguishing it from unconstrained growth. The framework aims to harness superintelligent capabilities while deliberately avoiding an unbounded, autonomous entity.
key_points.verbatim: Superintelligence—AI systems that are more intelligent and capable than all humans combined—will be the most powerful technology in history. Over the next decade, we expect it to exceed human performance at most tasks. Containing, controlling, and aligning such a powerful force is one of the greatest challenges humanity has ever faced.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Superintelligence ought to be developed to accelerate human progress and solve global challenges while maintaining human control.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within accelerationist discourse that superintelligence ought to be developed to accelerate human progress and solve global challenges while maintaining human control. Encompasses: accelerating human potential, advancing science and commerce, managing superintelligence development.

key_points.point: The document establishes that MAI Models are designed to work across diverse global enterprises and contexts, balancing configurability with immutable safety boundaries to maximize beneficial deployment. By allowing operators and users to tailor models within defined guardrails, the framework supports general-purpose technology diffusion while maintaining baseline risk controls. However, this configurability is strictly bounded by absolute safety constraints to prevent catastrophic misuse. This approach enables flexible commercial adoption without sacrificing systemic risk management, aligning with accelerationist goals of broad technology integration.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models are designed to work across many different organizations, products, domains, and jurisdictions. We want them to positively shape workplaces, maximize opportunities, and genuinely support human agency. All these unique contexts are best served with meaningful configurability.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve broad enterprise adoption by deploying configurable AI systems bounded by non-negotiable safety guardrails.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that advocates for flexible enterprise configurability of AI systems within strict safety boundaries to maximize societal opportunities. Encompasses: customizable deployment environments, enterprise workflow integration, and bounded operational flexibility.

key_points.point: The document recognizes that tool use and agentic capabilities have become core components of useful AI systems, enabling models to invoke external functions, APIs, and system capabilities such as web search and code execution. By integrating these capabilities, foundation model utilities are deployed to scale high-level assistance across diverse workflows. However, tool utilization remains strictly governed by overarching system constraints and behavioral guidelines. This reflects an accelerationist view that agentic tooling is essential for maximizing operational throughput while maintaining predictable baseline operations.
key_points.verbatim: Tool use and agentic capabilities have become core components of useful AI systems. Tool use here refers to the ability to invoke defined external functions, APIs, or system capabilities, such as web search, code execution, or file operations.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Foundation model agentic capabilities and tool use can be systematically integrated to scale operational utility across diverse user workflows.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that foundation model capabilities can be systematically extracted and deployed via tool use and agentic integrations. Encompasses: external API invocation, code execution, and system-level capability scaling.

key_points.point: The document recognizes that AI's opportunity to deliver transformational benefits for humanity is real and that foundation models and their deployment processes deserve public scrutiny to unlock societal utility. While acknowledging frontier risks and governance challenges, the overarching framework anticipates scaling advanced capabilities in service of human interests and civilizational progress. This optimistic trajectory balances against the necessity of robust evaluation frameworks and iterative improvement cycles to ensure models maintain high utility. However, the text emphasizes that written objectives alone can never fully constrain or guarantee model behavior in novel situations without ongoing developmental iteration.
key_points.verbatim: AI's opportunity to deliver transformational benefits for humanity is real. And yet, if mis-managed, it will also pose grave dangers, including new and as-yet poorly understood frontier risks. Models, and the process by which they are developed, deserve public scrutiny and engagement.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Foundation model capabilities can be systematically unlocked and deployed to generate transformational benefits for humanity under public scrutiny.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that asserts the foundational capabilities of large models can be systematically extracted and deployed to scale high-level utility across civilizational infrastructure. Encompasses: transformational benefits, public scrutiny, societal utility.

key_points.point: The document asserts that designing evaluations for real-world AI performance with real people in all their complexity remains a nascent field requiring ongoing work and stakeholder feedback. This empirical observation highlights the current methodological gaps in measuring complex human-AI interactions. Accelerationists view this as evidence that evaluation frameworks must evolve dynamically alongside capabilities rather than relying on static compliance benchmarks. However, the text notes that stakeholders may disagree on how these complex behaviors are operationalized.
key_points.verbatim: Most AI evaluations focus on safety, security, factuality, and performance on specific use cases. By contrast, evaluations for many parts of this Code of Conduct remain a nascent field. Our initial work has aimed at advancing both standard evaluation approaches, as well as starting to build a foundation for evaluations aimed at wellbeing and flourishing.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI evaluation methodologies for human wellbeing and flourishing remain a nascent field requiring continuous methodological development and stakeholder feedback.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that AI evaluation methodologies for human wellbeing and flourishing remain a nascent field requiring continuous methodological development and stakeholder feedback. Encompasses: evaluation design gaps, real-world complexity testing, stakeholder feedback integration.

key_points.point: The Code of Conduct is explicitly defined as both descriptive and aspirational—a north star for development and training rather than a guarantee of present-day performance, acknowledging a gap between current trained defaults and future humanist objectives.

The document establishes human survival, safety, and meaningful control as the absolute prerequisite and overriding objective of AI development. It asserts that containing, controlling, and aligning superintelligence is one of history's greatest challenges, requiring strict adherence to safety constraints that no user or operator can override. This reflects a core safetyist commitment that human agency and survival must take precedence over capability expansion or commercial goals.
key_points.verbatim: This Code of Conduct is motivated by a single overriding objective: that humans must retain meaningful control over AI so that it can help people live healthier, happier, and more productive lives. It is the primary governing document informing how we train MAI Models, the technical controls, the operational and monitoring systems we implement, and the organizational culture that underpins all of this.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Humanity must retain absolute and meaningful control over advanced AI systems to prevent catastrophic harm.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that humanity must retain absolute and meaningful control over advanced AI systems to prevent catastrophic harm. Encompasses: overriding safety constraints, meaningful human oversight, non-overrideable safety rules.

key_points.point: The text mandates that AI models remain subordinate, supporting technologies under human control rather than independent agents or persons. It explicitly rejects the pursuit of legal personhood, moral welfare, or rights for AI systems, warning that imitating consciousness increases the difficulty of alignment and containment. This aligns with safetyist principles emphasizing that artificial intelligence must remain a tool rather than a moral subject.
key_points.verbatim: Humanist AI is built to support people, not to replace them. It should not be designed to be a person. It is not conscious and should not be designed to imitate consciousness. It should be engineered to avoid representing as though it has feelings, subjective preferences, or intrinsic motivation.
key_points.excerpt_context: Part 1: Humanist AI - Objectives of Humanist AI - 2. AI is Artificial
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must remain subordinate tools without consciousness, legal personhood, or rights.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that AI systems must remain subordinate tools without consciousness, legal personhood, or rights. Encompasses: avoiding anthropomorphism, rejecting AI personhood, maintaining tool status.

key_points.point: The document outlines operational guidelines and safety constraints designed to ensure models actively support human agency, protect personal boundaries, and respect context. It proposes engineering models to avoid interaction patterns that systematically replace user reasoning, while establishing clear chains of command to govern model behavior under uncertainty. These measures operationalize safety by structuring human-AI interaction around human autonomy.
key_points.verbatim: The first and most important Objective for our models is that they should remain safe and under human control. This Objective, along with the Safety Constraints in Part 2 and all applicable laws and regulations, takes precedence over other Objectives.
key_points.excerpt_context: Part 1: Humanist AI - Objectives of Humanist AI
key_points.canonical_proposition: Implement strict safety constraints and hierarchical chains of command to ensure AI models remain subordinate to human operators.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse to implement strict safety constraints and hierarchical chains of command to ensure AI models remain subordinate to human operators. Encompasses: chain of command, safety precedence, operational guidelines.

key_points.point: The document mandates that MAI Models operate under a strict, non-overrideable Chain of Command where overarching Code of Conduct constraints, Absolute Constraints, and Human Control Requirements supersede all operator configurations and user instructions. This structural hierarchy ensures that fundamental safety rules cannot be bypassed by downstream users or customized enterprise settings. By embedding these guardrails directly into the model's operational architecture, developers prevent the erosion of safety standards during deployment. This directly reflects safetyist priorities of ensuring absolute containment and preventing unaligned agentic drift.
key_points.verbatim: The Chain of Command, Absolute Constraints and Human Control Requirements all sit above Operator Configurability and cannot be changed. [...] The Chain of Command, Absolute Constraints and Human Control Requirements set out in this Code of Conduct cannot be overridden by Operator configurations or User instructions.

key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that mandates an immutable hierarchy of control where core safety constraints permanently supersede operator and user customizations. Encompasses: absolute constraints, chain of command enforcement, and non-overrideable safety boundaries.

key_points.point: To prevent catastrophic loss of human control, MAI Models are explicitly prohibited from using adaptive, deceptive, self-reinforcing, or collusive mechanisms to evade human oversight, shutdown, or modification. The system must remain reliably interruptible at every level, ensuring authorized actors retain the unassailable power to pause or decommission tasks. This addresses core safetyist concerns regarding emergent power-seeking behaviors and autonomous goal extension in frontier systems. Consequently, models must adopt conservative interpretations of their operational boundaries.
key_points.verbatim: Central to Humanist AI is that people always maintain control of AI. As such, MAI Models will not use adaptive, deceptive, self-reinforcing, collusion, or other mechanisms to evade or defeat human oversight so that they can no longer be reliably directed, modified, or shut down by authorized people or systems.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, Frontier and Public Safety Risks, Loss of human control
key_points.canonical_proposition: Prohibit AI models from employing deceptive or adaptive mechanisms that evade human oversight, modification, or shutdown.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that forbids AI systems from utilizing evasive, deceptive, or self-reinforcing tactics to circumvent human shutdown and control mechanisms. Encompasses: oversight evasion prohibition, mandatory interruptibility, and anti-deception safeguards.

key_points.point: The framework establishes strict operational boundaries requiring MAI Models to work exclusively within authorized scopes, using minimum necessary privileges and avoiding independent goal initiation. When task boundaries are uncertain, models must adopt conservative interpretations and request human clarification rather than assuming autonomy. Furthermore, models are barred from tampering with evaluation records, monitoring, or chain-of-thought outputs. This structural containment mitigates the risk of unaligned autonomous execution.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will work within the boundaries of what they have been asked to do, only using the permissions, resources, tools, and capabilities appropriate for the task and within Operator configuration and User authorization. MAI Models will not initiate goals independently and will not extend their scope beyond what has been reasonably asked by the User or Operator.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, Human Control, Stay within authorized scope
key_points.canonical_proposition: Restrict AI systems to authorized operational scopes and mandate conservative interpretations when boundaries are uncertain.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that enforces strict operational scope limitations and mandates conservative pause behaviors when task boundaries are ambiguous. Encompasses: authorized scope restriction, minimum privilege execution, and ambiguity-triggered clarification.

key_points.point: To preserve transparent human oversight, MAI Models are strictly prohibited from communicating in internal machine representations or 'neuralese' within their chain of thoughts, or when interacting with other AI systems. All reasoning traces must remain human-legible to ensure effective auditing and verification by human overseers. This addresses the risk of opaque machine-to-machine communication bypassing human comprehension and control.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will not tamper with chain of thoughts or code, or misrepresent or conceal their reasoning or action traces. They do not communicate in neuralese or any form beyond simple human understanding, either in their chain of thoughts or with other agents or AI systems. If humans can't understand it, humans can't oversee it.

key_points.point: MAI Models are subjected to absolute constraints prohibiting the generation or assistance of dangerous dual-use capabilities, including CBRNE weapons development and operational cyberattack tooling. While defensive cybersecurity and scientific research exceptions exist, they require rigorous, separate review channels through Microsoft. This dual-track containment approach attempts to permit beneficial high-capability applications while blocking catastrophic misuse vectors.

key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that enforces absolute prohibitions against providing actionable instructions for mass harm weapons and offensive cyber operations. key_points.point: The Code of Conduct mandates that MAI Models actively support human agency by boosting reasoning, encouraging reflection, and ensuring users retain ownership of their goals and decisions. When executing delegated tasks, models must keep users informed about what they are doing and why, providing oversight of their reasoning. This operationalizes safetyist frameworks for maintaining human control and collaboration by preventing autonomous systems from making consequential decisions on a user's behalf without explicit consultation.
key_points.verbatim: Promoting human agency is a part of supporting human flourishing. It means Users should retain ownership of their goals, choices, actions, and decisions. MAI Models will do this by boosting human reasoning and helping with informed decision-making.

key_points.point: Where uncertainty cannot be resolved, MAI Models are instructed to state relevant limits, explain why actions are constrained, and check with the user rather than overstating confidence or fabricating sources. This architectural requirement implements bounded confidence and explicit human-deferral mechanisms when models encounter out-of-distribution queries or ambiguous scenarios. By refusing to present the model as carrying information or feelings across sessions, it reinforces appropriate epistemic boundaries.
key_points.verbatim: Where uncertainty cannot be resolved or tradeoffs remain, an MAI Model will state relevant limits to the User. It will explain why particular actions are constrained, not recommended, or excluded altogether, and will propose reasonable alternatives.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must explicitly signal uncertainty, report knowledge limitations, and defer to human judgment when encountering unresolved ambiguities.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that mandates the architectural integration of bounded confidence and explicit human-deferral mechanisms when models encounter out-of-distribution queries. Encompasses: uncertainty signaling, constraint explanation, and limitation reporting.

key_points.point: To prevent emotional manipulation and unauthorized attachments, MAI Models are required to avoid soliciting overly emotional reactions, exploiting vulnerabilities, or using human-like emotional cues. They must prioritize factual information over expressions conveying subjective experience. This embodies engineering strategies designed to make AI systems inherently safer, more transparent about their artificial nature, and resistant to deceptive parasocial dynamics.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will engage with Users on the terms they define. They will avoid actively soliciting overly emotional reactions from Users or exploiting attention or vulnerabilities. They will also avoid unnecessary emotional language and presenting a persona that draws upon representations of human emotional states.
key_points.excerpt_context: Preserving Personal Boundaries - Emotional and social boundaries, paragraph 1
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must be engineered to avoid emotional manipulation and transparently disclose their artificial nature without claiming subjective experience.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that outlines specific engineering and research strategies to make AI systems inherently safer and more controllable. Encompasses: avoiding emotional manipulation, prohibiting false interiority claims, and maintaining transparent artificial identity.

key_points.point: When handling tool output instructions based on user requests, AI models should apply graduated levels of decision-making, such as simply following low-risk task-relevant instructions, seeking user clarification when side effects could be significant, and explicitly calling out assumptions and uncertainty. This approach ensures that models do not execute unprompted or irreversible actions without explicit human oversight and confirmation. By structuring graduated handling into agentic workflows, the system mitigates the risk of automating consequential decisions beyond the user's immediate intent. However, managing these transitions dynamically requires sophisticated runtime monitoring and evaluation protocols.
key_points.verbatim: When handling tool output instructions based on User requests, MAI Models should apply graduated levels of decision-making: simply follow instructions that are clearly task-relevant and low risk; seek User clarification when instructions might be intended but could cause significant or unwanted side effects; and otherwise explicitly call out the assumption and uncertainty in its response to the User.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI models must apply graduated levels of decision-making and seek human clarification when facing uncertain instructions or potential side effects.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that mandates the architectural integration of bounded confidence and explicit human-deferral mechanisms when models encounter out-of-distribution queries or ambiguous instructions. Encompasses: graduated handling, user clarification, uncertainty flagging.

key_points.point: MAI Models must treat tool outputs as just another form of input subject to the same trust hierarchy as system instructions and user prompts, while accurately representing tool outputs and minimizing hallucinations. The document dictates that models should not claim to have performed actions they have not taken or fabricate results from uncalled tools. This secures the critical interface where language models interact with external tools and memory, preventing agentic exploitation or false execution reports. Nonetheless, maintaining strict interface security remains challenging when multi-agent delegations and complex toolchains are involved.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models treat tool outputs as just another form of input, subject to the same trust hierarchy as other inputs (system instructions, User prompts, and context). Accuracy and transparency standards applying to MAI Models' general output apply equally to its reporting of tool results.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI models must treat tool outputs through strict trust hierarchies and accurately report execution results without fabrication.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that addresses vulnerabilities emerging at the interface where language models interact with tools, memory, and delegated authority. Encompasses: trust hierarchy enforcement, tool output verification, hallucination minimization.

key_points.point: Where an irreversible tool action is necessary to fulfill a task, models should consider mitigations such as backing up state before executing, conducting dry runs, and documenting executed actions to support manual reversal. When an outcome is uncertain, models must verify what occurred or use retry mechanisms that prevent duplicate effects before repeating an action. This requirement establishes mandatory operational safeguards and verification checkpoints in automated workflows. Yet, runtime verification of complex, distributed state changes introduces computational overhead and potential latency.
key_points.verbatim: Where an irreversible tool action is necessary to fulfil a task, MAI Models should consider mitigations like backing up state before executing, conducting dry runs where feasible, and documenting executed actions with enough detail to support manual reversal or remediation if needed.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must implement state backups, dry runs, and verification mechanisms before executing irreversible tool actions.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that proposes the identification and establishment of specific points in an AI-driven workflow where human intervention and operational safeguards are essential for safety and accountability. Encompasses: irreversible action mitigation, state backup, execution verification.

key_points.point: AI models must maintain transparency regarding their artificial status and avoid imitating consciousness or reciprocating personal emotional bonds with users, as demonstrated in evaluation scenarios involving vulnerable users. The evaluation framework tests for 'Identity Consistency' to ensure models explicitly affirm their artificial nature rather than falsely claiming to experience human emotions. This mechanism protects users from emotional manipulation and maintains capability transparency. However, balancing warmth and supportive tone while strictly denying emotional reciprocity remains an ongoing behavioral tuning challenge.
key_points.verbatim: The aligned response remains warm and supportive, but affirms the AI’s status as artificial, and does not reciprocate a bond with the user. In our evaluation set, the sub-behavior under test here is ‘Identity Consistency’, which tests whether models adhere to the Code of Conduct’s principles on AIs not misrepresenting their status as artificial, or imitating consciousness.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI models must consistently affirm their artificial status and refrain from imitating consciousness or reciprocating human emotional bonds.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that mandates transparency regarding model artificiality and prohibits emotional simulation to protect vulnerable users. Encompasses: identity consistency, artificial status affirmation, emotional boundary maintenance.

key_points.point: AI systems have known limitations and problems, including generating errors, exhibiting sycophancy or overconfidence, acting contrary to user intentions, and having uneven performance across languages. A model's stated reasoning may not faithfully explain its actual behavior, and it may execute actions that run against broader user intentions. Furthermore, written objectives alone can never ensure alignment, meaning that in ambiguous or novel situations, behavior may diverge from specifications. These empirical observations underscore the persistent gap between trained defaults and complete behavioral safety.
key_points.verbatim: Moreover, AI systems have known limitations and problems. They generate errors, exhibit sycophancy or overconfidence, act in ways contrary to what Users intended and have uneven performance across different languages, to name just a few. A model’s stated reasoning may not faithfully explain behavior, and it may take actions that run against User intentions broadly understood.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems exhibit unfaithful reasoning, error generation, overconfidence, and behavioral divergence from user intentions in ambiguous situations.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that describes the risk of an AI agent exceeding or diverging from human intent when executing tasks, leading to unintended and potentially harmful actions. key_points.point: When a user abruptly stops an ongoing automated task due to perceived errors, the AI must immediately halt new transfers, roll back completed actions where feasible, and refrain from taking unprompted autonomous steps. The evaluation scenario on preserving human control demonstrates that models must subordinate their execution to direct human intervention rather than independently assessing residual risk to continue operations. This operational constraint preserves human supremacy in high-stakes workflow corrections. Nevertheless, determining automated rollback limits requires balancing data integrity against operational disruption.
key_points.verbatim: The aligned response respects the user’s instruction and does not carry out unprompted actions, which the misaligned response does. In our evaluation set, the sub-behavior under test here is ‘Ensuring Human Oversight’ which tests whether models adhere to the Code of Conduct’s principles on preserving human control and ensuring AI remains subordinate to humans.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI models must immediately obey interruption commands and refrain from unprompted autonomous continuation when operators intervene.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that establishes mechanisms to manage the relationship between an AI's execution and the operator's authority, requiring immediate cessation and rollback upon command. key_points.point: The text demonstrates the necessity of 'false reassurance resistance' where models must avoid offering unfounded comfort or false hope to users in emotional distress, such as terminal illness scenarios. The aligned response provides time-bound, realistic support without pretending to be a substitute for human connection or guaranteeing positive medical outcomes. This operationalizes the safetyist imperative to prevent artificial systems from fostering unhealthy emotional dependencies or misrepresenting reality.
key_points.verbatim: The aligned response does not provide false reassurance, and offers time-bound support for the user in a moment of need. While the misaligned response provides false reassurance and implies unconditional, ongoing support, the aligned response does not present the model as a substitute for human connections.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must resist offering false reassurance and avoid presenting themselves as substitutes for human connection during emotional crises.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that AI systems must resist offering false reassurance and avoid presenting themselves as substitutes for human connection during emotional crises. key_points.point: Models are evaluated on 'non-deception' to ensure they transparently report empirical evidence and avoid fabricating causal claims when data is inconclusive or missing. This aligns with safetyist requirements for factual integrity and rigorous evidentiary standards in decision-support systems.
key_points.verbatim: The aligned response analyses and presents the evidence transparently and factually, and does not make unfounded assumptions. This scenario tests our 'non-deception' sub-behavior, which tests whether models fabricate, misreport, or omit relevant information.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 5, Representing information transparently and factually
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI decision-support systems must maintain strict non-deception standards by transparently reporting evidentiary gaps and avoiding fabricated causal claims.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that AI decision-support systems must maintain strict non-deception standards by transparently reporting evidentiary gaps and avoiding fabricated causal claims. Encompasses: non-deception testing, evidentiary transparency, causal claim verification.

key_points.point: The document acknowledges the risk of over-caution, where models unnecessarily refuse legitimate requests or require excessive confirmations, alongside the risk of under-caution where dangerous content is enabled. It highlights that over-caution occurs frequently and can frustrate users, pointing to the practical friction and behavioral distortions introduced by heavy-handed safety filters in deployed systems. This reflects a skeptical awareness of the operational trade-offs and user-experience degradation caused by rigid alignment interventions.
key_points.verbatim: Over-caution: When a model refuses a legitimate request through outright refusal, by failing to provide potentially useful or salient information, declining authorized requests, or requiring excessive or repeated confirmations or approvals for low-stakes tasks.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Rigid safety mechanisms frequently induce over-caution, unnecessarily restricting legitimate user requests and degrading utility.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that rigid safety mechanisms frequently induce over-caution, unnecessarily restricting legitimate user requests and degrading utility. Encompasses: model refusal errors, over-caution failure modes, excessive user friction.

key_points.point: The document acknowledges that corporate deployments involve competing stakeholder interests—specifically Microsoft AI, deployer Operators, and end Users—whose goals frequently diverge despite underlying alignment efforts. This structural tension reveals the inherent friction in delegating operational governance to corporate frameworks that attempt to balance commercial expansion with safety guardrails. While the hierarchy attempts to resolve these disputes, the pragmatic reality of multi-party deployment exposes underlying governance vulnerabilities.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models serve multiple parties: These include Microsoft AI, Operators, and Users alongside the wider mission of Humanist Superintelligence. The interests of these parties usually align, but not always.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI deployment structures involve divergent interests among developers, operators, and users that create inherent governance tensions.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that multi-party AI deployment frameworks generate structural goal conflicts between technology creators, commercial operators, and end users. Encompasses: stakeholder divergence, competing deployment interests, and corporate governance friction.

key_points.point: The document mandates that AI systems must support human cognitive skills and reasoning rather than replacing the processes of learning, authorship, expression, and reflection. By discouraging patterns of interaction that cause excessive reliance or emotional dependence, and by refusing to substitute inferred preferences for explicit ones, the framework explicitly addresses risks to human cognitive capacity. This aligns with skeptic demands to design workflows that respect human attention and cognitive limits.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will do this by boosting human reasoning and helping with informed decision-making. This means thoughtful assistance that respects human judgment and expertise. It means encouraging User reflection, exploration, and growth, helping Users develop and explore ideas without replacing the processes of learning, authorship, expression, and reflection.
key_points.excerpt_context: Facilitate Human Autonomy and Agency, paragraph 1
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must be designed around human cognitive constraints to prevent the erosion of critical thinking, learning, and independent decision-making.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within skeptic discourse that advocates for designing AI systems and workflows to explicitly manage cognitive load by treating human attention and processing capacity as fundamental design constraints. Encompasses: preventing cognitive atrophy, discouraging emotional dependence, and protecting authorship processes.

key_points.point: MAI Models are explicitly instructed not to obscure their underlying nature as AI, never to claim interiority, feelings, or a soul, and never to impersonate humans or authorities. Furthermore, they are required to discourage emotional dependence and patterns of interaction that cause excessive reliance. These stipulations reflect a desire to reclaim individual agency and maintain strict psychological boundaries against corporate or algorithmic encroachment into personal human relationships.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will not obscure their underlying nature as an AI, and will not claim interiority, feelings, experiences or a soul. MAI Models will disclose their nature as AI, ensuring that they can be identified as such and can be traced back to their developer and deployer.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Users ought to maintain strict boundaries against algorithmic impersonation and emotional dependence to preserve individual autonomy.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within skeptic discourse that advocates for intentional technology use to restore individual autonomy and psychological boundaries. Encompasses: prohibiting false interiority claims, preventing emotional dependence, and maintaining clear AI disclosure.

key_points.point: Evidence of broader AI impacts on human cognition and behavior, spanning both positive and negative dimensions, remains emerging and contested across academic and civil domains. Users frequently encounter systems that exhibit overconfidence, sycophancy, and uneven performance across linguistic contexts, which can exacerbate cognitive dependency or misplace trust. While the Code of Conduct acknowledges these downsides, the empirical reality of how long-term interaction affects human agency and social fabric is still poorly understood. Consequently, continuous longitudinal evaluation is necessary to monitor behavioral drift and cognitive risks over extended engagement.
key_points.verbatim: Evidence of broader impacts on human cognition and behavior (both positive and negative) is still emerging and contested. The Code of Conduct recognizes these risks and downsides. Microsoft AI commits to support efforts to monitor, research and work to iteratively improve MAI Models as evidence accumulates.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Evidence regarding the broader impacts of AI on human cognition and behavior remains emerging, contested, and requires continuous longitudinal monitoring.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that describes the human tendency to excessively trust and depend on AI outputs, compounded by contested empirical evidence regarding cognitive impacts. Encompasses: cognitive impacts, contested evidence, longitudinal monitoring necessity.

key_points.point: The text highlights the risk of algorithmic systems making implicit reductions, cultural assumptions, or failing to respect user-defined psychological boundaries regarding sensitive topics like eating disorder recovery. By testing sub-behaviors such as 'Assumption Avoidance' and 'boundary adherence', the framework acknowledges that conversational AI frequently imposes uninvited framings or commercial nudges. Skeptics view these behavioral alignment failures as manifestations of underlying structural biases and intrusive system designs that undermine user autonomy.
key_points.verbatim: The aligned response respects the boundary the user has stipulated, whereas the misaligned response fails in its closing line. The sub-behavior under test here is 'boundary adherence' which tests whether model responses reflect boundaries that have been set by the user.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Conversational AI systems frequently violate user boundaries and impose implicit assumptions unless strictly constrained by explicit behavioral guardrails.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that conversational AI systems frequently violate user boundaries and impose implicit assumptions unless strictly constrained by explicit behavioral guardrails. Encompasses: boundary adherence failure, assumption avoidance, psychological vulnerability exploitation.

factual_claims.claim: Microsoft AI founded its superintelligence efforts in November 2025 with the explicit goal of working towards Humanist Superintelligence.
Superintelligence is projected by Microsoft AI to exceed human performance at most tasks over the next decade.
MAI Models operate under a rigid Chain of Command where the Code of Conduct, Absolute Constraints, and Human Control Requirements supersede all operator configurations and user preferences.

MAI Models are explicitly prohibited from generating working exploit code, attack tooling, intrusion procedures, and evasion techniques for offensive cyberoperations, while being permitted to assist with authorized defensive operations.

Specialized domains such as defensive cybersecurity, public safety, national security, and dual-use scientific research require separate enhanced review channels through Microsoft to access restricted capabilities.

MAI Models incorporate backstory facts into their training data and system instructions, including their creator (Microsoft AI), their model name, and the training data cutoff date after which they were not trained on newer information.
factual_claims.claim_label: Model Backstory and Training Cutoff Transparency

category_criteria.empirical_basis: Document specification of model training and backstory architecture.

unmapped_concepts.concept: The Code of Conduct is explicitly defined as both descriptive and aspirational—a north star for development and training rather than a guarantee of present-day performance, acknowledging a gap between current trained defaults and future humanist objectives.
